niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, markets, creative needs, and whether you want programmatic scale or boutique CTV expertise.

To give a useful recommendation, tell me:
- Primary objective (brand awareness, direct response, app installs, lead generation, etc.)
- Monthly/quarterly budget range
- Geographic market(s) (US, EMEA, APAC, global)
- Need for end‑to‑end service (strategy, media buying, creative, measurement) or just one function
- Any preferred platforms (Roku, Amazon Fire TV, LG, Samsung, Apple TV)
- In‑house data/tech you want to use (DMP/CRM, identity graphs, first‑party data)

If you want immediate options, here’s a short framework + vetted agency options by type to help you decide.

How to pick a CTV partner (quick criteria)
- Scale & platform access: Can they buy across Roku, Hulu, FAST channels, publisher inventory and through major DSPs (Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, Magnite)?
- Measurement & attribution: Do they use independent third‑party measurement (Samba TV, iSpot, IAS), and can they do exposed vs. control lift studies?
- Creative capabilities: Do they produce CTV‑native spots, dynamic/interactive creatives, and A/B test variants?
- Data & targeting: Can they ingest your first‑party data, apply household/segment targeting, and integrate identity solutions?
- Transparency & reporting: Clear breakdown of media fees, tech fees, and viewability/post‑view metrics.
- Case studies & vertical experience: Proven results in your industry and on similar KPIs.

Agency options by type (examples)
- Large global/full-service (best for scale, brand campaigns, cross‑channel planning):
  - GroupM (Mindshare, Wavemaker, MediaCom)
  - Omnicom (OMD, PHD, Hearts & Science)
  - Dentsu (Dentsu X, Amplifi)
  - Publicis (Spark Foundry, Starcom)
  - IPG (UM, Initiative, MAGNA)
  Pros: scale, buying leverage, cross‑channel planning. Cons: potentially higher minimums, less boutique attention.

- Programmatic/tech‑forward DSPs & platforms (best for advanced audience targeting & performance):
  - The Trade Desk (DSP)
  - Amazon DSP
  - Magnite / Xandr derivatives / SpotX sellers
  - Roku OneView (platform + ad products)
  Pros: deep programmatic reach and control. Cons: you may still need creative/strategy partner.

- CTV specialist agencies & performance-focused shops (best for focused CTV campaigns or direct response):
  - MNTN (formerly SteelHouse) — performance‑oriented CTV buying + creative
  - Tinuiti — strong performance marketing + CTV
  - Mediahub — creative + activation with TV focus
  - Tremor / Tremor Video (now within broader programmatic ecosystems) / Amobee (ad tech + agency)
  Pros: CTV expertise, creative formats, fast execution. Cons: less cross‑channel muscle than holding companies.

- Creative & measurement specialists:
  - Innovid (creative personalization + measurement)
  - Samba TV, iSpot — for measurement and attribution partners (not agencies, but important vendors)
  - Independent creative boutiques that specialize in long‑form/CTV creative

Questions to ask any prospective CTV agency
- Which CTV platforms and inventory sources do you buy (publisher direct, programmatic, platform-based)?
- Can you run exposed/control lift tests and share independent measurement?
- How do you handle audience targeting and can you onboard our first‑party data?
- What are your typical CPMs and fee structure (media vs. technology vs. management)?
- Do you create CTV‑native video and interactive units? Can you localize/adapt creative?
- Can you show case studies with KPIs similar to ours?

Next step
If you share your goals, budget, market and whether you need full service or specific services (creative, media buying, measurement), I’ll recommend 2–3 agencies that fit your needs and include a brief rationale for each.
